title: Fourier-nonexceptional middle extension
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, as in [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. A lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf is understood in the finite-extension adic convention of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] supplies its finite-ring lisse convention. A lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $U_0$ is a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $U=U_0\otimes k$ in this convention (its underlying geometric sheaf, written $\mathcal M|_U$) together with a Weil descent datum $\varphi:\Phi_U^*\mathcal M|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal M|_U$ along the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $\Phi_U$, as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. No comparison of this lisse model with another coefficient model is used: the condition below depends only on the underlying lisse sheaf on $U$.

Let $\psi:(k_0,+)\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ be an additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion and
let $\mathcal M$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$ (in the lisse convention
of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]). Its middle extension
$j_*\mathcal M$ is *Fourier-nonexceptional* if, after geometric base
change, it is neither a constant sheaf (up to a constant Weil twist,
which does not change the underlying sheaf) nor the Artin–Schreier sheaf
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] for any $a\in k$.
Using $j^*j_*\mathcal M=\mathcal M$, this is the following condition on
$U=U_0\otimes k$: $\mathcal M$ is not geometrically constant (its
underlying sheaf on $U$ is not constant), and for no $a\in k$ is
$\mathcal M$ geometrically irreducible with $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ as
a geometric constituent (equivalently, $\mathcal M|_U\cong\mathcal
L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$, the Artin–Schreier sheaves being irreducible).
Here $j_*\mathcal M$ is the ordinary sheaf-theoretic middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension], and constant Weil twists are those of [def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. Geometric constancy has the meaning of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Geometric constituents have the Jordan–Hölder meaning of [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]; geometrically irreducible means that the underlying lisse sheaf on $U$ is nonzero and has no nonzero proper lisse subsheaf, with no Weil structure imposed on the subsheaf. For $a\in k$, $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ is the pullback of the underlying geometric sheaf $\mathcal L_\psi$ along multiplication $x\mapsto ax$ on $\mathbf A^1_k$, as in [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. For this arbitrary $\psi$, $\mathcal L_\psi$ on $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ is the $\psi$-isotypic component $e_\psi\cdot(\mathrm{AS}_q)_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of the push-forward along the Artin–Schreier map $\mathrm{AS}_q:x\mapsto x^q-x$, the construction of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] for the character $\psi$ of the finite field $k_0$. The quantifier includes $a=0$. No irreducibility hypothesis on $\mathcal M$ and no nontriviality hypothesis on $\psi$ is imposed in this definition.
